channel.title: Omong Studio
channel.description: A working journal from Omong Studio: how AI short-form episodes get made, how music videos are timed to the beat, and how one-file apps get shipped. Real pipelines, no hype.

item.title: One Vertical Ad, Two Languages: Localising Captions and Voiceover Without Re-Cutting the Picture
item.description: A client approves the Korean cut and then asks for English. The picture should not move. A per-line sheet, a reading-speed budget for each language and a delivery package built around a silent master keep it that way.

item.title: Activation in Seven Days: The One Event, the Funnel Maths and the Churn Interview
item.description: Sign-ups arrive every day and the product is empty by week three. The fix is not a longer tour: it is one activation event, a median time to value, four emails with one action each — and the maths that says how many paying customers that is worth.

item.title: A Product Page for a Digital Download: Eight Sections, Eighteen Objections and the Test Maths
item.description: A listing with views and no sales is usually answering the wrong question, in the wrong order. Eight sections in the order a buyer asks them, the objections that block a $19 download, and the sample size a test needs before it can tell you anything.

item.title: Matching Colour Across AI Shots: Measure Four Numbers, Grade in Two Passes, Then Apply the Look
item.description: Six AI clips cut together can look like footage from six cameras. The fix is not a better LUT — it is measuring four numbers per clip and grading in the right order, so one look survives a whole series.

item.title: What a 15-Second Ad Costs to Make Alone: Hours, a Rate Floor and a Quote That Holds
item.description: Two quotes for the same 15-second vertical ad can differ by ten times and both be honest. What separates them is whether the person quoting knows where the hours go — so here are the hours, the rate floor they imply, and the six lines a quote needs before it leaves your desk.

item.title: What One Workflow Run Really Costs: Run-Cost Math, Retry Budgets and Rate-Limit Guardrails in n8n, Make and Zapier
item.description: Two workflows that do the same job can cost ten times different amounts, and both can fail at 3am without telling anyone. The billing unit each platform counts, the retry window it gives you, and the guardrails that make a run safe to leave on.

item.title: Editing 9:16 Shorts for Retention: the Hook Frame, Caption Rhythm and the Loop Point
item.description: A vertical short is lost or kept in the first 1.5 seconds and at the last 1.5. Everything between them is caption rhythm and cut cadence — three things you can set before the first render.

item.title: AI Talking Heads That Don't Slip: Lip-Sync Timing, Jaw Artifacts and Three Failure Modes
item.description: Lip-sync does not fail all at once. It drifts four frames over eight seconds, or the jaw walks through the teeth on the first plosive. Both are fixable before the render.

item.title: Thirty Vertical Videos a Month From One Spreadsheet: a Batch Pipeline That Survives Week Three
item.description: Daily uploads do not fail on day one. They fail on day nineteen, when the script, the voice file and the shot folder stop matching. One spreadsheet column fixes that.

item.title: Packaging a Digital Kit for Gumroad: File Structure, a Price Ladder and Delivery That Refunds Itself
item.description: A prompt pack is not a product until a stranger can open the ZIP and know what to do in ninety seconds. The structure, the price steps and the listing copy that does the selling.

item.title: Suno Stems for a 60-Second Ad: Generate the Bed, Split It, Cut Picture to the Beat
item.description: A commercial bed is not a song with thirty seconds deleted. Generate it in sections, split it into stems, and rebuild sixty seconds whose cuts land on the beat — not near it.

item.title: Mastering Audio for Faceless YouTube and AI Podcasts: LUFS Targets, Chain Order and a Per-Line Voiceover Workflow
item.description: A faceless channel is an audio product with pictures attached. Four numbers keep forty episodes at the same level, and one chain order keeps the voice sounding like the same show.

item.title: Building a Cinematic AI Music Video Pipeline in 2026: Audio, Visuals & Voiceover Timing
item.description: Most AI music videos are cut to a storyboard that has nothing to do with the song. Start from the timecode map instead, and every other stage gets shorter.

item.title: How to Keep AI Characters Consistent Across 9:16 Short-Form Episodes (3-View Sheets & Motion Transfer)
item.description: The face starts drifting by episode three. A three-view character sheet, a frozen descriptor block, and one action per clip are what held a nine-episode vertical series together.

item.title: Shipping Solo-Creator Micro-Tools Fast: Why Single-File Offline HTML Apps Win
item.description: One HTML file, no build step, no server, no login. For a solo creator selling small tools, that constraint is not a limitation — it is the whole product advantage.
